skill.name: image-inpainting
skill.description: Run mask-driven image inpainting jobs on RunComfy with the runcomfy CLI. The skill helps remove or replace masked regions, choose the right edit model, and set inpainting parameters.
skill.summary: Run precise image inpainting and local image edits through RunComfy.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documentation links, placeholder URLs, and explanatory text. The real security surface is limited to intentional runcomfy CLI execution and outbound uploads to RunComfy, plus a semantic misuse risk from explicit watermark-removal guidance.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution is required for the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the allowed tool scope limited to Bash(runcomfy *) and avoid recommending arbitrary shell scripts or unpinned remote installers.

remediation.issue: User images and masks are sent to a remote model service.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should not submit confidential images unless they accept RunComfy processing and retention terms.

remediation.issue: Watermark removal can support rights abuse.
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad watermark-removal language with guidance limited to marks the user owns or is authorized to remove.

content.value_statement: Precise image edits are hard when only one region should change. This skill routes Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to RunComfy inpainting models with mask-aware prompts and safe CLI usage.
actual_capabilities: Runs RunComfy inpainting jobs with source image, mask image, prompt, strength, and control scale inputs.
Recommends Z-Image Turbo Inpainting when a binary mask is available.
Routes no-mask edits to description-based image edit models such as Nano Banana 2 Edit, GPT Image 2 Edit, or FLUX Kontext Pro.
Provides parameter guidance for retouching, object replacement, and full region replacement.
Explains expected CLI exit codes and troubleshooting categories.
limitations: Requires the runcomfy CLI, an authenticated RunComfy account, and network access.
Mask-driven inpainting requires a separate image mask URL.
The skill does not create masks inside the workflow.
Generated quality depends on the source image, mask quality, model choice, and prompt clarity.

use_cases.title: Clean product photos
use_cases.description: Replace a masked background or remove a small defect while preserving the product shape and lighting.

use_cases.title: Repair image regions
use_cases.description: Fill a damaged or empty area using a mask and a prompt that describes the desired replacement.

use_cases.title: Localize visual edits
use_cases.description: Use description-based editing when a mask is not available but the target region can be named clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Remove a masked object
prompt_templates.prompt: Inpaint this image using the provided mask. Remove the masked object and preserve the background texture, lighting, and perspective.

prompt_templates.title: Replace a masked background
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mask to replace only the background with smooth light gray studio paper. Preserve the product edges, shadows, and color.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the best edit route
prompt_templates.scenario: Model selection before running a job
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an image and this edit goal, but I am not sure if my mask is good enough. Choose the best RunComfy inpainting or edit route and explain the needed inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Tune an inpainting job
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an inpainting job for this masked region. Use a lower strength for subtle repair, set control scale for edge preservation, and include a reproducible seed.

output_examples.input: A user provides a street photo and a cable mask, then asks to remove only the overhead cables.
output: The skill selects Z-Image Turbo Inpainting because a mask is available.
It prepares a prompt that preserves rooflines and sky gradients.
It runs the job through the runcomfy CLI and saves outputs to the chosen directory.

output_examples.input: A user has no mask but wants the bottom-right label removed from an image they own.
output: The skill chooses a description-based edit model.
It writes a spatial instruction that targets only the bottom-right label.
It reminds the user to confirm they are authorized to remove the mark.

output_examples.input: A product team wants a masked background changed to a neutral studio backdrop.
output: The skill recommends high strength for full background replacement.
It preserves product edges and lighting in the prompt.
It uses the supplied image and mask URLs for the RunComfy request.

best_practices: Use a clean grayscale mask where white marks the region to change and black marks the region to preserve.
Name the surrounding details that must stay unchanged in every prompt.
Use only images and marks you own or have permission to edit.
anti_patterns: Do not use a vague prompt that fails to describe what should remain unchanged.
Do not reuse a mask from a different source image.
Do not submit private or regulated images unless remote processing is approved.

faq.question: Does this skill create masks?
faq.answer: No. It consumes mask URLs created by another tool, such as an image editor or segmentation workflow.

faq.question: Which model is used by default?
faq.answer: The skill prefers Z-Image Turbo Inpainting when a mask is available.

faq.question: Can it edit images without a mask?
faq.answer: Yes. It can route to description-based edit models when the region can be described clearly.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI and remote model APIs, so network access is required.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: The runcomfy CLI writes generated files to the output directory selected in the command.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential images?
faq.answer: Only use confidential images if your organization approves remote processing through RunComfy.
